Best AI research and search tools in October 2026

Tools that search the web, read papers and documents for you, and answer with sources you can check. Below are the 18 that Raunak picked, in Radar's order, then the most popular of the other 496 in this category on Radar.

  1. 1PerplexityAsk anything, get an answer written from the web with every source cited.Free plan
  2. 2NotebookLMTurns your own documents into a notebook you can question, and a podcast about them.Free
  3. 3ElicitFinds the papers on a question and pulls the findings out into a table.Free plan
  4. 4ConsensusAnswers questions from peer-reviewed studies, and shows how far they agree.Free plan
  5. 5Semantic ScholarAi2's search engine for scientific papers, with one-line summaries of each.Free
  6. 6Kagi AssistantThe ad-free search engine's assistant: the big models, grounded in Kagi's results.Paid
  7. 7You.comSearch and research agents that write up what they find, with citations.Free plan
  8. 8SciSpaceReads papers with you: explains passages, compares studies and drafts literature reviews.Free plan
  9. 9SciteShows how a paper has been cited, supported, disputed or just mentioned.Paid
  10. 10ResearchRabbitMaps the papers around the ones you care about, and keeps you posted on new ones.Free
  11. 11Connected PapersA visual graph of the papers related to any one you start from.Free plan
  12. 12UndermindA research agent that reads hundreds of papers to find the ones that really answer you.Free plan
  13. 13LinerAn AI search engine for students and researchers, with trustworthy sources.Free plan
  14. 14FeloMultilingual AI search that can turn its answers into slides and mind maps.Free plan
  15. 15ChatPDFUpload a PDF and ask it questions; answers point back to the page.Free plan
  16. 16HumataAsk questions across long documents and get cited, page-linked answers.Free plan
  17. 17Julius AIA data analyst you talk to: upload spreadsheets, get charts and answers.Free plan
  18. 18Wolfram|AlphaComputes answers, maths, science, data, rather than searching for them.Free plan

Free to start: Perplexity, NotebookLM, Elicit all have a free plan or are free outright.
